3._section_summary: This section describes the testing of a hypothesized structural model with 249 participants using Mplus maximum likelihood estimation. The authors controlled for BMI's contribution to five model variables (restrictive/critical caregiver eating messages, attachment anxiety, depressive symptoms, body appreciation, and intuitive eating) and examined multiple fit indices (CFI, SRMR, RMSEA) to evaluate model adequacy. The final revised model achieved good fit and revealed that body appreciation was predicted by restrictive/critical caregiver eating messages, attachment anxiety, and perfectionism dimensions, with body appreciation and other variables together predicting 44.4% of variance in intuitive eating.
